procedures.title: Identidade do serviço e aquisição pela superfície pública
procedures.preconditions: Two synthetic isolated service instances and a declared trusted-context adapter; public exports resolved without deep imports.
steps: Acquire the same instance through two context views.
Replace it with a distinct instance.
Compile a valid public-consumer fixture and negative fixtures with a required export/member removed.
procedures.required_observation: Same-instance views preserve identity; replacement differs. All required mapped public declarations exist; abstract service is not represented as an executable storage backend.
procedures.discriminating_negative_control: Adapter that creates a new identity per access, reuses identity after replacement, or exposes only a private deep import must fail.
procedures.actual_boundary_required: Public composition identity and compile-time/public-package resolution; does not prove durable IO.

procedures.title: Create, colisão, ausência e visibilidade local
procedures.preconditions: An empty disposable backend, two unique synthetic IDs, fixed valid current-format headers, and explicit process-instance identity.
steps: Create S and await its returned write handle.
On the same instance stat/list/open-read S before any append.
Try a second create of S, open absent T, and stat T.
procedures.required_observation: S is locally visible when create resolves; write access is granted; duplicate create is a distinct exists failure; open T is not-found and stat T is undefined. No cross-process pre-materialization visibility is required.
procedures.discriminating_negative_control: Upsert masquerading as create, accidental creation on open/read, hidden S until first append, or stat returning a phantom session fails.
procedures.actual_boundary_required: Actual backend service visibility. In-memory-only execution cannot establish later crash durability.
procedures.acceptance: Both valid and known-bad controls must be observed on exact separately authorized candidates; no source/API-name/test-count parity credit.

procedures.title: Header imutável e corte herdado fora do log
procedures.preconditions: Current-format synthetic header factories and a seeded/unseeded fork fixture with exact declared inherited prefix N.
steps: Create an unseeded S with omitted/zero inherited cut and a seeded F with an explicitly supplied safe nonnegative N; test independently declared N0/N1/N2 values.
Try an omitted seeded cut, negative/noninteger cut and nonzero cut for an unseeded header.
Mutate caller-owned header data after invocation; inspect handle/read metadata and event log.
procedures.required_observation: Stored header is detached from caller mutation, bound to the addressed identity and fixed for the handle. The supplied cut is retained exactly as storage metadata. It need not equal the parent log length and is not inferred from currently appended events; a seeded zero cut is not rejected merely for being zero. No synthetic header/cut event is inserted into the replayable event stream.
procedures.discriminating_negative_control: Alias-mutable header, seeded missing cut/unseeded nonzero cut silently accepted, changing the declared cut to current event count, or an invented metadata event in the log fails.
procedures.actual_boundary_required: Validated create and logical session body metadata; persisted-byte/source protocol versions remain distinct.
procedures.acceptance: Both valid and known-bad controls must be observed on exact separately authorized candidates; no source/API-name/test-count parity credit.

procedures.title: Single writer e leitores concorrentes
procedures.preconditions: One materialized synthetic session; two independent owned processes or native backend clients and a controlled start barrier.
steps: Keep read handles open while competing A/B request write access.
Observe exactly one successful write owner and the other typed already-owned refusal.
Read while writer remains active; try append/flush through a read handle.
procedures.required_observation: Write claim is atomic and exclusive; read does not acquire or displace ownership; read mutations fail read-only without changed log.
procedures.discriminating_negative_control: Check-then-set admitting two owners, read blocking solely because a writer exists, or read handle mutation must fail.
procedures.actual_boundary_required: Native shared ownership state across the backend boundary; an in-process fake lock is insufficient for cross-process claim.
procedures.acceptance: Both valid and known-bad controls must be observed on exact separately authorized candidates; no source/API-name/test-count parity credit.

procedures.title: Perda de ownership não ressuscita o handle

steps: Obtain write handle A; deterministically invalidate its ownership through the declared backend mechanism.
Attempt append and flush on A; close it and explicitly reopen a new handle after legal ownership recovery.
procedures.required_observation: Lost A cannot reacquire implicitly or mutate; a distinct reopened handle is required. Error export existence is tested separately even if native loss capability remains unknown.
procedures.discriminating_negative_control: A stale handle refreshing its own ownership or writing after another owner takes over must fail. No synthetic thrown error can count as native fencing evidence.
procedures.actual_boundary_required: Real native lease/ownership record when supported; reference capability availability remains NOT_VERIFIED until executed.

procedures.title: Append contíguo e preservação do prefixo
procedures.preconditions: A valid current-format event factory, initial next-seq0, write ownership and raw/logical observation of the original prefix.
steps: Append [0,1] and [2,3] in order.
Try a gap, a reordered batch and a batch starting below the committed next-seq.
Read the complete log and compare the original prefix.

procedures.discriminating_negative_control: Sorting, dropping, silently overwriting or accepting a discontinuous batch must fail. Compare exact ordered event identities and payloads; normalizing lost/extra events is forbidden.

procedures.title: Snapshot lossless dos dados aceitos
procedures.preconditions: Bounded plain synthetic objects, fixed safe createdAt, separate invalid JSON vectors, and a fixed own-enumerable getter witness whose successive reads return two valid JSON literals. Observe the original getter at an in-process input boundary before any transport serialization. Admission is statically supported by snapshotJsonValue, which validates own enumerable keys then reads each original property once; actual runtime admission remains NOT_RUN.
steps: First separately confirm reference materializer admission of the fixed plain getter witness; unexpected refusal is REFERENCE_ADMISSION_DIVERGENCE, never a silent acceptance-rule change.

For header.agentPreset use a fixed own enumerable getter with reads counter: first returns synthetic-A, second synthetic-B. Invoke materializeCreateHeader synchronously; require one original-property read and snapshot synthetic-A. For append event.data.turn use the same bounded pattern0 then1, requiring one read and captured0.

Run the synchronous known-bad control that validates the original once then copies the original in a second traversal before any await. It reads twice/capturesB and must fail the one-read/capturedA oracle even though both values are type-valid.
Repeat through the actual local create/append route with the witness installed at the same original-input boundary. A JSON-serialized witness is not this test.
Independently retain the ordinary-data test: invoke create/append, mutate caller-owned nested data while backend work is pending, then compare accepted stored metadata/events.
Apply invalid JSON and invalid createdAt vectors to helpers and actual write route.
procedures.required_observation: The validated snapshot is exactly what storage receives. The admitted fixed getter is read once from the original and its first value is captured; synchronous check-then-copy cannot pass just by finishing before caller mutation. The separate pending-IO case rejects later alias mutation. Lossy/non-JSON values and invalid createdAt fail before persisted mutation. This is a controlled local observation, not containment of arbitrary getters or Proxy code.
procedures.discriminating_negative_control: The synchronous two-original-traversal control must be rejected by reads2/capturedB; the alias-after-await control must separately be rejected by changed stored data. Silently erasing invalid data or allowing invalid createdAt also fails. Do not substitute asynchronous mutation alone for the single-capture oracle.
procedures.actual_boundary_required: Input materialization plus real append/create route; a copied validator alone does not prove storage wiring.

procedures.title: Read por segmento e propriedade dos valores
procedures.preconditions: A valid log [0,1,2,3], exact offset/length projection and independent read handles.
steps: Read default/full, offset1 length2, offset at/past end, and an empty valid session.
Mutate the returned outer array; reread.
Check eventState detached/shared-frozen: any actually shared alias must be deeply frozen; independently owned unfrozen values may coexist under shared-frozen. Empty slices retain the producer state.

A shared-frozen result may mix frozen shared aliases with independently owned unfrozen values, as the core type explicitly permits; do not require every value frozen or every backend cloning.

procedures.title: Freshness entre handles com happens-before explícito
procedures.preconditions: Two handles on the same backend instance; an explicit acknowledgment barrier for append/flush resolution and read-start trace.

Only then start B.read and stat/list; repeat after flush.
Repeat reads on the same handle after growth; separately record a read that was concurrent with mutation.

procedures.title: Flush é a barreira de durabilidade
procedures.preconditions: Disposable real durable backend and owned child A/B with fixed IPC acknowledgments; no existing user session path. Candidate/tool/resource hashes recorded under a future execution authorization.
steps: A creates empty S and awaits handle.flush; acknowledge resolution, terminate A and reopen from a distinct process B.
Repeat with an exact accepted event prefix followed by flush.
Record an unflushed crash separately without demanding that unflushed events be lost.
procedures.required_observation: After a resolved barrier, empty session metadata and all acknowledged appends survive process death and are readable in B. A backend that persists eagerly is allowed; absence of a flush method in a proposed adapter remains a contract gap until a justified equivalent is specified.
procedures.discriminating_negative_control: Known-bad adapter acknowledging flush while retaining data only in memory must lose data across A/B and be rejected. Same-process recreation or graceful close cannot prove crash durability.

procedures.title: Close e asyncDispose: drenar, liberar, rejeitar operações futuras
procedures.preconditions: Owned read/write handles, pending accepted appends and an independently observable backend owner record.
steps: Close a writer with pending accepted data; reopen elsewhere and verify prefix/ownership release.
Call close repeatedly and through Symbol.asyncDispose; close a reader.
After close try read/append/flush and observe no resource leaks.
procedures.required_observation: Close is asynchronous/idempotent/uncancellable, drains writer durability and releases ownership; reader frees only local resources. Other closed operations fail typed-closed; close itself remains idempotent.
procedures.discriminating_negative_control: Close that discards accepted data, leaves ownership active, blocks repeated disposal or accepts post-close mutation must fail.
procedures.actual_boundary_required: Actual teardown and durable/ownership completion, bounded process/stream/resource join.

procedures.title: Flush global agrega falhas sem abandonar demais sessões
procedures.preconditions: Two active write handles A/B, one read handle, and a declared test-only failure seam at A storage durability; no arbitrary production function substitution.
steps: At global-flush invocation record the active-write set.
Cause A native flush to fail while B can succeed; close one captured writer concurrently.
Inspect aggregate failures and restart-read B; verify the reader is untouched.
procedures.required_observation: Every captured active writer is attempted; close-concurrent counts as durable drain. AggregateError identifies failed sessions, and other writers complete their barriers despite A failure.
procedures.discriminating_negative_control: Fail-fast behavior that skips B, a generic unnamed error or calling flush on the read handle must fail.

current_gaps.observation: CVG public SessionEventStore exposes openSession/append/read, no per-session read/write handle or matching service create/open/flush/stat/list/dispose contract.
Public context identity/exports and typed reference error categories need an explicit versioned CVG bridge; no alias by similar name proves parity.
CVG SessionStream carries tenantId/sessionId/formatVersion, without the immutable header/snapshot metadata promised by the reference contract.
CVG openSession is idempotent; reference create rejects duplicates, and absent stat/open semantics differ. No silent upsert substitution.

Reference logical seq starts0 and has its own current format; CVG event sequence starts1 and read is afterSequence-exclusive. A lossless explicit projection is required; numeric renumbering is not interoperability.
Operational execution leases217 do not establish session-handle single-writer ownership/release semantics.
OwnershipLostError is exported, but its documentation notes declared cross-process-layer availability. Selected backend behavior needs execution, not inference from the export.
CVG per-event digest/deduplication differs from exact caller-supplied contiguous batch seq and required event vocabulary validation; design and differential evidence pending.
CVG read returns only an array, without eventState/read-handle monotonicity semantics. Existing validation/fresh objects are static leads, not functional evidence.
No corresponding public stat/list/opaque revision contract exists on current SessionEventStore.

PG per-append transaction may satisfy a stronger durability point, but handle/global flush, empty-session materialization and close barriers need explicit mapping and native crash tests. In-memory store cannot prove cross-process durability.
Current SessionEventStore options lack signal parameters and service-wide flush/partial failure contract.

CVG schema fingerprints/format registry/error codes require a lossless contract for reference refusal/corruption/physical-tail semantics. Historical formats/migration are still outside this finite proposal.
